activities.title: Four jobs words can do
activities.instructions: Read the overview and notice where each word class appears.
activities.content: NOUNS name people, places, things or ideas. VERBS express actions or states. ADJECTIVES describe nouns. ADVERBS describe verbs, adjectives or other adverbs.

activities.title: See the pattern
activities.instructions: Read the sentence and compare the related word forms.
activities.content: The efficient assistant organized the files quickly. Assistant is a noun; organized is a verb; efficient is an adjective; quickly is an adverb.

activities.title: Identify the word class
activities.instructions: In the sentence “The manager spoke confidently,” what kind of word is confidently?
activities.content: Choose the word class that best describes “confidently.”
activities.explanation: Confidently describes how the manager spoke, so it modifies the verb and is an adverb.

activities.title: Choose the correct form
activities.instructions: Choose the best word to complete the sentence.
activities.content: Our customer service team responds ______ to all inquiries.
activities.explanation: The blank modifies the verb responds, so the adverb promptly is required.

activities.title: Complete the sentence
activities.instructions: Type the correct form of the word in brackets.
activities.content: The new scheduling software has improved office ______. (efficient)
activities.explanation: After the verb improved, the sentence needs the noun efficiency.

activities.title: TOEIC sentence completion
activities.instructions: Select the option that makes the sentence grammatically correct.
activities.content: Employees must obtain written ______ before purchasing new equipment.
activities.explanation: The adjective written needs to modify a noun. Approval is the noun form.

activities.title: Repair the error
activities.instructions: Rewrite the incorrect word in its correct form.
activities.content: The board was complete satisfied with the quarterly results. Which word should replace “complete”?
activities.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective satisfied.

activities.title: Mini review: position clues
activities.instructions: Use position clues when you are unsure of a word form.
activities.content: Before a noun, expect an adjective. After an article, expect a noun or adjective + noun. After a linking verb, expect an adjective. To describe an action, use an adverb.

activities.title: Short quiz
activities.content: The marketing department created an extremely ______ campaign.
activities.explanation: The blank describes the noun campaign, so the adjective effective is correct.

activities.title: Lesson summary
activities.instructions: Check that you can apply all four ideas before continuing.
activities.content: You can now identify the four major word classes, use sentence position as a clue, select the correct related word form, and explain why an answer fits a TOEIC sentence.

activities.title: Skim before you scan
activities.instructions: Read the title and first sentence of each paragraph to predict the main idea.
activities.content: Urban gardens are becoming an important part of city planning. They provide fresh food, cool public spaces and places where neighbors can meet.

activities.title: Part A: Academic Writing Task 1
activities.instructions: Study two complete bar-chart models, build the key language, then complete guided and independent practice.
activities.content: Write at least 150 words. Select the main features, include a clear overview and support comparisons with accurate figures.

activities.title: Part B: Writing Task 2
activities.instructions: Study two complete opinion-essay models, build the key language, then plan and write your own response.
activities.content: Write at least 250 words. State a clear position, develop relevant reasons and support them with examples.

activities.title: A clear 30-second introduction
activities.instructions: Prepare, then speak for 30 seconds without reading.
activities.content: Introduce yourself, say what you study or do, and describe one reason you are learning English.

activities.title: The sentence core
activities.instructions: Find the subject and the main verb in each example.
activities.content: A complete English sentence normally needs a subject and a finite verb: “The class starts.” Extra information can be added after this reliable core.
